## Natural history notes

A large foliose lichen characterized by broad, ruffled gray to bluish-gray lobes, a pale underside, and powdery or granular reproductive patches along the lobe edges and surface. In Florida, it is found growing on tree bark, branches, and sometimes weathered wood in humid forests, hammocks, swamps, parks, and shaded yards where air moisture is high. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, growing flat or loosely attached to bark and absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air.
